questions.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type I region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{{e}^{x}}^{e}\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡y}{y}\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}x[{\int }_{{e}^{x}}^{e}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡y}{y}\,dy]\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}x{[\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡y}{2}]}_{{e}^{x}}^{e}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}x(\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡e}{2}-\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡{e}^{x}}{2})\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}x(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{1}x(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})\,dx & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2})\,dx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{-2}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{4}-\frac{(-2)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(-2)^{4}}{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{4}-2+4) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{2-1-8+16}{4}) \\  & =\frac{9}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over the type I region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,\frac{1}{x}\le y\le \frac{3}{x}\}.$

So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{2}{1+4{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,dA & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1/x}^{3/x}\frac{2}{1+4{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1/x}^{3/x}\frac{2}{1+4{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{1/x}^{3/x}\frac{2}{1+(2xy)^{2}}\,dy]\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{[\frac{1}{x}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2xy)]}_{1/x}^{3/x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2))\,dx \\  & =(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2)){\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2)){\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x}\,dx & =(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2))[\operatorname{ln}⁡x]_{1}^{2} \\  & =(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2))\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1) \\  & =(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2))\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type I region. 

- To determine the $x$-limits, we need to find the $x$-coordinates of the points at which the curves intersect. So, we set the following equation and solve it for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x} & =e \\ x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x$-limits are 
$0\le x\le 1.$

- To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272737/assets/95a6d9b0bc464c719311dc900967ebd06a3aa3d3004cfe5303359eecb20551e7.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{e}^{x}\le y\le e\}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{e}^{x}}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $y=2-x$ and $y=4-{x}^{2},$ then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's make a sketch of our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272737/assets/600f11ddc0f26dc0f70e2970da6d5a5737e7eac64cf6aa2d18faf589e243c307.png)

Now, let's represent $D$ as a type I region. 

- To determine the $x$-limits, we need to find the $x$-coordinates of the points at which the curves intersect. So, we set the following equation and solve it for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2-x & =4-{x}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}-x-2 & =0 \\ (x-2)(x+1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x$-limits are 
$-1\le x\le 2.$

- To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272737/assets/41af03028d6c780f9b13464c314c7094e78996068a862ef8ac3ca8b6af8067a0.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 2,\,2-x\le y\le 4-{x}^{2}\}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{2-x}^{4-{x}^{2}}f(x,y)\text{ }dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}[{\int }_{2-x}^{4-{x}^{2}}f(x,y)\text{ }dy]dx\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3x}{x}^{2}\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{3x}\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}[\,y\,]_{0}^{3x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}(3x-0)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{x}^{3}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}3{x}^{3}\,dx & ={[\frac{3{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3(1)^{4}}{4}-0 \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
